🔐 ChatGPT's always-on agents can now grab login codes from your email and sign in for you

OpenAI's dots, the agents that keep working in their own cloud browser after you log off, can now use the one-time sign-in codes a website sends to your connected inbox.

When a code is needed, you choose: let the dot use it once, or always allow it to fill codes in. The demo shows a dot logging into the restaurant app Resy with the user's email.

Those codes exist to prove it's really you. So far, OpenAI's help page has told users to complete that kind of check themselves or take over the dot's browser.

James Sun, who works on browser use for ChatGPT and Codex at OpenAI, announced the change. He says "lots more sign-in improvements" are coming soon.

Dots are rolling out to Pro users outside the European Economic Area, the UK and Switzerland, plus Business Premium and Enterprise workspaces.
